column4: user-excluded
Closed DataValue query forms preserve all upstream validation branches and exact errors on Native and Melange.
Closed return-map variants preserve keys, syms, strs, find-shape checks, counts, and exact errors on Native and Melange.
Closed query inputs preserve upstream arity validation and exact binding-source errors on Native and Melange.
Native covers empty, small, large, incremental, lazy restore, index caching, settings, and equality behavior; read-count assertions follow the shared upstream CLJS PSS control flow used by LG.
Native exercises every upstream format case through the concrete typed Storage_value codec boundary, both Strong and Weak policies, branching factors 32/64/512, and empty/small/large databases.
Native deterministically verifies live-address retention, orphan deletion, root/tail retention, and avoids relying on garbage-collector timing.
Native preserves initial storage, transaction tails, overflow flushes, restored transactions, garbage collection, and repeated connection restoration.
Melange covers empty, small, large, incremental, lazy restore, index caching, settings, and equality behavior with exact upstream CLJS read counts.
Melange replays cardinality-one tail datoms, restores stored tails, rejects conflicting unique groups atomically, and advances max transaction IDs.
Melange preserves initial storage, transaction tails, overflow flushes, restored transactions, and repeated connection restoration.
Closed tuple schema values preserve upstream validation and error behavior on Native and Melange.
Derived tuple maintenance preserves upstream add, update, retract, and direct-modification behavior on Native and Melange.
Direct tuple assertions are ignored only when their source attributes already match, as upstream requires.
Unique tuple constraints and tuple update conflicts match upstream on Native and Melange.
Tuple identity upserts, conflicts, and derived tuple updates match upstream on Native and Melange.
Stable closed auto tempids preserve upstream retry behavior when tuple components resolve an existing entity.
Tuple lookup refs in transaction entity ids preserve upstream resolution, conflict, and update behavior.
Reference-valued tuple components accept numeric and nested lookup refs and resolve them as upstream does.
Partial and nil tuple values retain upstream direct-modification validation behavior.
Tuple values preserve upstream EAVT, AEVT, AVET, and VAET index behavior.
Tuple constants, tuple lookup refs, tuple construction, and untuple binding match upstream query behavior.
Closed entity refs and values preserve upstream upsert resolution, conflicts, retry behavior, refs, cardinality-many values, and current transaction handling on Native and Melange.
Repeated and conflicting tempid definitions preserve upstream allocation and error behavior on Native and Melange.
Retry state preserves upstream transaction ordering on Native and Melange.
String tempids used as ref values and later resolved by upsert match upstream on Native and Melange.
Multiple tempids and repeated upsert retries preserve upstream resolution state on Native and Melange.
Vector transaction upserts preserve upstream identity resolution on Native and Melange.
Closed tx-entry forms cover every representable upstream validation branch; malformed raw shapes are rejected statically, and Native/Melange preserve runtime errors.
Unique-value conflicts and non-conflicting attributes match upstream on Native and Melange.
